item.title: Marathi polar question particles and (non-)canonicity of questions
item.dc:creator: Kulkarni, Aaditya
item.description:
Kulkarni, Aaditya · LingBuzz

In this paper, I describe syntax and semantics of Marathi polar questions and polar questions particles to place them on the broader Indo-Aryan landscape. In doing so, I argue that Marathi polar question particles uniformly signal information-seeking polar questions when clause-final, while their clause-medial occurrences – wherever grammatical – signal non-canonical questions of various kinds. I show that this indicates a strict mapping between the syntactic and semantic-pragmatic notions of canonicity of questions and necessitates a closer examination of semantic-pragmatic properties of clause-medial polar question particles from Indo-Aryan languages previously described in the literature.

item.dc:creator: Anna Prysłopska
item.description:
Anna Prysłopska · PsyArXiv

This paper introduces CoBra, a Corpus of German Bracketing Paradox Phrases, and describes its construction. It characterizes CoBra as a specialized linguistic resource that can be used both as a source of attested examples for theoretical work on adjective-compound modification and as an experimentally grounded dataset, in which each phrase is linked to the aggregated results of five psycholinguistic experiments on adjective attachment. It explains how these envisioned uses informed the compilation process. CoBra comprises 913 attested adjective-compound phrases drawn from sources published between 1822 and 2026, and is freely available for academic use.
